purpose: Curated source/evidence boundaries for Phase-3 semantic relations. Evidence scopes are intentionally narrower than possible narrative interpretations.

supports: Landgrave Carl developed the Baroque water display.
Carl appointed Giovanni Francesco Guerniero to take charge of the design after his Italy tour.
Wilhelm IX continued to employ Heinrich Christoph Jussow, Daniel August Schwarzkopf and the water engineer Steinhöfer.

sources.publisher: State Party nomination dossier / UNESCO World Heritage Centre
supports: The upper Baroque water-display ensemble, including Hercules Monument, Octagon and Grand Cascade, was built under Landgrave Carl in 1689-1717.
Giovanni Francesco Guerniero supervised the upper works from October 1701.
The Aqueduct and Devil's Bridge waterfalls are attributed to Heinrich Christoph Jussow together with water engineer Carl Steinhöfer.
Steinhöfer alone is identified as responsible for the Steinhöfer Waterfall and the New Waterfall.
Landgrave Carl chose Hercules as a symbol of his power and had the giant Hercules statue erected.
The whole Hercules Monument is described as 70 m high; this is physical monument height, not terrain elevation.

sources.publisher: Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel / architecture drawings catalogue
supports: Giovanni Francesco Guerniero is the named architect of a 1713 Octagon design drawing.

sources.publisher: Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel / architecture drawings catalogue
supports: Guerniero's 1713 pyramid design was part of his construction contract and the catalogue states that the final Kassel work he supervised was executed from this drawing through 1714.
The Hercules sculpture itself was installed in 1717; the catalogue does not establish Guerniero as sculptor of the statue.

sources.publisher: Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel / architecture drawings catalogue
supports: Heinrich Christoph Jussow is the architect of the first Aqueduct design drawing, dated before 1789.
This particular first design was not executed because it was too expensive, so it must not alone be treated as proof that the extant Aqueduct exactly follows GS 5846.

sources.publisher: Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel / architecture drawings catalogue
supports: Jussow's drawing documents the landscape/watercourse from Devil's Bridge through Hell Pond toward the Aqueduct around the early Romantic redesign.

sources.publisher: Museumslandschaft Hessen Kassel / architecture drawings catalogue
supports: A circa-1791 design context for Pluto Grotto and Devil's Bridge is attributed to Jussow with catalogue-level uncertainty (fraglich/questioned).
Heinrich Christoph Jussow began planning Löwenburg while shaping the Wilhelmshöhe park in the English style.
The Kassel Old Masters collection contains twelve Rembrandt paintings and explicitly names Der Segen Jakobs among the best-known works on display.
The Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister has been located in Schloss Wilhelmshöhe since 1974.
